body.input: and emotional robotics platform.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: And what I saw in Sophia was a way to get AI algorithms

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: out there in front of a whole lot of different people

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: in an emotionally compelling way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: And part of my thought was really kind of abstract,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: connected to AGI ethics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: And many people are concerned AGI is gonna enslave

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: or whatever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: And emotionally, I'm not driven to that sort of paranoia.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: I'm really just an optimist by nature,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: but intellectually, I have to assign a non-zero probability

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: to those sorts of nasty outcomes.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: Because if you're making something 10 times as smart as you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: how can you know what it's gonna do?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: There's an irreducible uncertainty there,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: just as my dog can't predict what I'm gonna do tomorrow.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: So it seemed to me that based on our current state

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: of knowledge, the best way to bias the AGI's we create

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: toward benevolence would be to infuse them

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: with love and compassion the way that we do our own children.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: So you want to interact with AIs in the context

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: of doing compassionate, loving and beneficial things.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: And in that way, as your children will learn

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: by doing compassionate, beneficial,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: loving things alongside you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: and that way the AI will learn in practice

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: what it means to be compassionate, beneficial and loving,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: it will get a sort of ingrained intuitive sense of this,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: which it can then abstract in its own way

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: as it gets more and more intelligent.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: Now, David saw this the same way.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: But I think most of it will be there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: And these will be incarnations of your consciousness

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: in a slightly different flavor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: And creating these different versions will be amazing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: And each of them will discover meanings of life

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: that have some overlap,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: but probably not total overlap

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: with the human Ben's meaning of life.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: The thing is to get to that future

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: where we can explore different varieties of joy,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: different variations of human experience and values

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: and transhuman experiences and values.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: To get to that future,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: we need to navigate through a whole lot of human bullshit

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: of companies and governments and killer drones

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: and making and losing money and so forth, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: And that's the challenge we're facing now

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: is if we do things right,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: we can get to a benevolent singularity,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: which is levels of joy, growth and choice

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: that are literally unimaginable to human beings.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: If we do things wrong,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: we could either annihilate all life on the planet,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: or we could lead to a scenario where say,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: all humans are annihilated

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: and there's some super AGI that goes on

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: and does its own thing unrelated to us,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: except via our role in originating it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: And we may well be at a bifurcation point now, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: Where what we do now has significant causal impact

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: on what comes about.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: And yet most people on the planet

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: aren't thinking that way whatsoever.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: They're thinking only about their own

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: narrow aims and goals, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: Now, of course, I'm thinking about my own narrow aims

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: and goals to some extent also,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: but I'm trying to use as much of my energy and mind as I can

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: to push toward this more benevolent alternative,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: which will be better for me,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: but also for everybody else.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: And it's weird that so few people understand what's going on.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: I know you interviewed Elon Musk

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: and he understands a lot of what's going on,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: but he's much more paranoid than I am, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: Because Elon gets that AGI is going to be

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: way, way smarter than people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: And he gets that an AGI does not necessarily have to give a shit

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: about people because we're a very elementary mode

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: of organization of matter compared to many AGI's.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: But I don't think he has a clear vision of how infusing early stage AGI's

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: with compassion and human warmth can lead to an AGI

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: that loves and helps people rather than viewing us as,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: you know, a historical artifact and a waste of mass energy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: But on the other hand, well, I have some disagreements with him.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: Like he understands way, way more of the story

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: than almost anyone else in such a large-scale corporate leadership position, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: It's terrible how little understanding of these fundamental issues

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: exists out there now.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: That may be different five or ten years from now though,

body.input: because I can see understanding of AGI and longevity and other such issues

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: is certainly much stronger and more prevalent now than ten or fifteen years ago, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: So I mean, humanity is, as a whole, can be slow learners relative to what I would like,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: but on a historical sense, on the other hand,

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: you could say the progress is astoundingly fast.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: But Elon also said, I think on the Joe Rogan podcast, that love is the answer.

metadata.title: Podcast: Ben Goertzel: Artificial General Intelligence | Lex Fridman Podcast #103

body.input: So maybe in that way, you and him are both on the same page

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: "'Hey, let's make a basic program

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: "'that does the Death Star trench run.'"

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And it was just simple 2D graphics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And I didn't know what I was doing,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: so I just helped him out on the math and stuff like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: I was a math and science kid.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: I was really into the HP calculators of the early mid-70s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: These were the RPN.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: They were really strongly built,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and it was all right goldfinger instead of gold,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: divinely heavy.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: There's probably some gold in them too, gold metalization.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: But they were awesome calculators,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and they had all the scientific functions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: so I was really into that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: So I aimed towards physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: I was a little late for the, I think,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: the 20th century golden age,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and I read a lot of science fiction,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: so I was like, yeah, it's on the hybrid drives

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and warp drives, and physics was not gonna get there quickly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And I started hacking on computers

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: while I was studying physics as an undergraduate

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: at Santa Clara University.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And I dodged the Fortran bullet

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: because I was in the science department

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: instead of the engineering department

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: where they still did Fortran card decks.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: I think they had an autocollator.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: But we were using Pascal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and I got one of the first portable C compilers ports

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: to the deck mini computers we were using.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And I fell in love with programming just based on, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: procedural abstraction, Pascal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: just what now would be considered old school,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: like structured programming from the 70s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Niklaus Wirth, the creator of Pascal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: was a good writer and a good pedagogue, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: He always at ETH would do these courses

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: where it's like build your own computer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: build your own compiler, build your own operating system.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: It was gratch.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Yeah, kind of.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And I know some people who were grad students under him

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and said he would torture the students

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: with things like this custom email system

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: that had 25 word limit.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: I unfortunately dodged both the Pascal

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and the Fortran bullets.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Could you maybe linger on the Pascal?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Like what kind of programming language was it?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: What is it reminiscent of today?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Because it sounds like it may have had an impact

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: on your own trajectory.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Yeah, it was in the Algo family.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And Algo was the big successful language design

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and compiler project in the 60s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: It had a successor called Algo 68,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: which was ambitious, but not as successful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: But Pascal was kind of a wordy procedures

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and functions language.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: It distinguished between functions,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: which are a turn of value, and procedures, which don't,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: which just compute.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And you could say that whole Algo family went into Ada.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Pascal had a second life thanks to Borland with Turbo Pascal,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: which was hugely successful.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: I think in large part due to Anders Halsberg,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: who then went to Microsoft and did C Sharp

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and done that with his team there.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: He's done really well doing TypeScript, TypeJavaScript.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: So yeah, there's a lineage here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: But I was also interested in C and Unix

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: by the time I was an undergrad,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: because people were bringing Unix up

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: on all sorts of hardware.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: I had some friends who were doing

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: their own wire wrap computers, 6820 maybe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And I was wire wrapping for my engineering course,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: 6809 or something simpler, building a computer on a board.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And I wanted to build a more ambitious one

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and port Unix to it, but I picked the wrong processor.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: I picked the National Semiconductor NS16032,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: which was this amazing, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: CISC complex instructions set computer,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and not the reduced instructions set computers

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: that were just being contemplated into the mid-80s.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And RISC ultimately went out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: RISC won in some ways, it dissolved into,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: you have both now, you have these superscalar architectures

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: where like Intel has kept probably too much

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: backward compatibility at the instruction level,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: but that's just, there's a front end that parses that

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: into these wide internal instructions.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: So, you know, the very long instruction word research

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: that was also interesting at the time

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: kind of became the micro architecture

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: inside the backward compatible Intel.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: But I picked the National Semi chip

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and it never got made successfully.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: It was full of bugs and I never could have brought it up.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: But I went on out of physics after three years

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: into math computer science.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And like I said, I did it because I saw,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: I was being sort of childlike and naive about physics

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and I thought, meanwhile, the Valley is go-go for computers.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: The Apple II, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: The PC, the Intel 8086, 8088 based PC,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: the IBM gave Microsoft the future for,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: in a somewhat fishy deal.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: So it was wide open in the computing space, but in physics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: you were as optimistic about physics as-

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: No, I mean, I was one of three brothers

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: who were all in the same grade.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: I have a twin and a younger brother who skipped second grade

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and was with us the whole time after that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And he went on, he actually studied

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: under Kip Thorne at Caltech.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: But he also ended up at software.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: He didn't talk about physics.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Does it make you sad that theoretical physics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: even with string theory,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: hasn't really had any foundational breakthroughs

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: in the latter part of the 20th century and today?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Yeah, in fact, I'd say the problem is theory over experiment.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: I would say we need more Aristotle and less Plato.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Mathematics is not all physical.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: There are lots of mathematics that cannot be realized

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: as far as I know in this world.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: So to understand the world, you need to do experiments.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: You need to not just dream up inductive theories

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: that could have lots of alternative theories

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: competing with them with no way to decide between them

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: except aesthetics, which is not a good guide in my opinion.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: I don't know if you are friends with,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: have a relationship with Elon Musk.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Where's the, in terms of like what you would love to see

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: our society investing in building up?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Is it closer to Elon or is it closer to Feynman

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and Einstein and those?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Well, those gentlemen are no longer with us.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And I think that's noticed.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: So like I said, the real glory days of physics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: the famous pictures from Germany before the second war

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: were just a fantastic assembly of brains,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Schrodinger and Einstein.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Physics, I think, took a wrong turn

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: that maybe all of, I would say, Western science

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: took in going for models over reality, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: You see this in all sorts of fields.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Now we can build models that are very predictive

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and generative and then we build actual devices

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: or semiconductors, things like that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: That's good, I'm not dismissing that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: We need good models.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: We need to experiment and prove them and test them.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: But the problem I've seen in physics,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: which you see certainly in economics, the dismal science,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and you see surprisingly in other so-called hard sciences

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: is models that don't really have to be tested

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: against reality.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: They can instead become policy tools or they can become,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: like I said, one of a large family of alternate theories

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: that could be as predictive,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: but nobody's doing the winnowing out.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: That's such an interesting tension in society.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: You see this in even the softer sciences,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: which I have a deep love for, like psychology.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: You see this in epidemiology, not with the virus.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: This tension of how much of the world can we understand

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: as part of our tooling.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: So when I realized that these accidents,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: like the third party cookie,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: the image or script that's tracking you,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: or the JavaScript that can do it invisibly now,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and that Firefox had supported extensions

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: that block some of these things,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: just block some of these things by default.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: These were not intended and they're now unsafe.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: They're tracking you, there could be data breaches,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: malware distribution, bullying and PSY ops

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and other attacks on people.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Block that stuff, block that JavaScript.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: I'm Dr. Frankenstein, I've got to deal with a monster here.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: from unrelated domains or apparently unrelated domains.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and machine learning practice around blocking.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And at Brave, we did that from the start

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and built a research team to help drive it and automate it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: We realized that protecting people needed machine learning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And around 2017 spring, I talked to my friends at Apple

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: which uses local machine learning in the browser.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And the funny thing is, you know,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: great minds think alike,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: that was in Safari from the old days

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: and making it not have a big loophole.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Because what they did was in 2003, when Safari came out,

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: that cookie would not be set.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: And that was a real move for privacy early on

body.input: when jobs were still around in Safari.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: then why it's okay to be a third party cookie.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: was sophisticated enough to counteract this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: or even possibly get an ad revenue share for private ads

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: Some people have this sort of model

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: you have limited choices.

metadata.title: Podcast: Brendan Eich: JavaScript, Firefox, Mozilla, and Brave | Lex Fridman Podcast #160

body.input: but in being able to take advantage of the other player and figure out where they're

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: were making good money.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: Then what really solidified it, I think, was the Labratas match where we played our bot

body.input: When I was in grad school, there was this thing called the annual computer poker competition

body.input: It was trying to say, okay, well, let me in real time try to compute a much better strategy

body.input: And that's kind of hard to wrap your head around.

body.input: And the idea is, again, you want to always be balanced and unpredictable.

body.input: And so if your search algorithm is saying, oh, I want to raise with this hand, well,

body.input: in order to know whether that's a good action, let's say it's a bluff.

body.input: So if your action in some sense maximizes your unpredictability, so that action could

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: Basically what you want to do is put your opponent into a tough spot.

body.input: And if you are raising in the appropriate balance between bluffs and good hands, then

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: And so that's what we're trying to do.

body.input: We're always trying to search for a strategy that would put the opponent into a difficult

body.input: Does this have to do with the regret thing that we're talking about in terms of putting

body.input: your opponent in a maximally tough spot?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: Yeah, ultimately what you're trying to maximize is your expected winnings, like your expected

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: value, the amount of money that you're going to walk away from, assuming that your opponent

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: was playing optimally in response.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: So you're going to assume that your opponent is also playing as well as possible a Nash

body.input: Anything that deviates, by definition, the Nash equilibrium is the strategy that does

body.input: And so if you're deviating from that, then they're going to lose money.

body.input: And since it's a two player zero sum game, that means you're going to make money.

body.input: This is too real.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: Okay.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: That's fascinating.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: So that cooperation element is what makes the game really, really hard.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: So just to give you an example of how this suboptimality and irrationality comes into

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: play, there's a really common situation in the game of diplomacy where one player starts

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: to win and they're at the point where they're controlling about half the map.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: The remaining players who have all been fighting each other the whole game all have to work

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: together now to stop this other player from winning or else everybody's going to lose.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: And it's kind of like Game of Thrones.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: I don't know if you've seen the show where you got the others coming from the North and

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: all the people have to start, work out their differences and stop them from taking over.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: And the bot will do this.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: The bot will work with the other players to stop the superpower from winning.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: But if it's trained from scratch or it doesn't really have a good grounding in how humans

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: approach it, it will also at the same time attack the other players with its extra units.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: So all the units that are not necessary to stop the superpower from winning, it will

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: use those to grab as many centers as possible from the other players.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: And in totally rational play, the other players should just live with that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: They have to understand like, hey, a score of one is better than a score of zero.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: So okay, he's grabbed my centers, but I'll just deal with it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: But humans don't act that way, right?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: The human gets really angry at the bot and ends up throwing the game because I'm going

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: to screw you over because you did something that's not fair to me.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: Got it.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: And are you supposed to model that?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: Is the bot supposed to model that kind of human frustration?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: Yeah, exactly.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: And so that is something that seems almost impossible to model purely from scratch without

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: any human data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: It's a very cultural thing.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: And so you need human data to be able to understand that, hey, that's how humans behave and you

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: have to work around that.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: It might be suboptimal, it might be irrational, but that's an aspect of humanity that you

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: have to deal with.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: So how difficult is it to train on human data given that human data is very limited versus

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: what a purely self-play mechanism can generate?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: That's actually one of the major challenges that we faced in the research that we had

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: a good amount of human data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: We had about 50,000 games.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: What we try to do is leverage as much self-play as possible while still leveraging the human

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: So what we do is we do self-play very similar to how it's been done in Poker and Go, but

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: we try to regularize the self-play towards the human data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: Basically the way to think about it is we penalize the bot for choosing actions that

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: are very unlikely under the human data set.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: And so-

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: How do you know?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: Is there some kind of function that says this is human-like and not?

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: Yeah.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: So we train a bot through supervised learning to model the human play as much as possible.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: So we basically train a neural net on those 50,000 games, and that gives us a policy that

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: resembles to some extent how humans actually play the game.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: Now this isn't a perfect model of human play because we don't have unlimited data.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: We don't have unlimited neural net capacity, but it gives us some approximation.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: Yeah, absolutely.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: So we are able to leverage the wider data set in order to fill in some of the gaps in

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: how communication happens more broadly besides just specifically in these diplomacy games.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: Okay, cool.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: So what are some interesting things that came to life from this work to you?

body.input: Well, I think there's a few insights.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: And that is, I think, applicable more broadly to a lot of different games.

metadata.title: Podcast: Noam Brown: AI vs Humans in Poker and Games of Strategic Negotiation | Lex Fridman Podcast #344

body.input: So I'm a social psychologist,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: which means I study how we think about other people

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: I picked the topic of moral psychology,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: and I studied how morality varied across countries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: And in the 90s, I began,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: And in that decade was really when the American culture war

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: And I began to notice that left and right in this country

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: were becoming like separate countries.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: And you could use the tools of cultural psychology

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: to study this split,

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: So I started doing that.

body.input: And I began growing alarmed in the early 2000s

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: And I began studying the causes of polarization,

body.input: bringing moral psychology to bear on our political problems.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: because I could see that some of my research showed

body.input: people on the right understand people on the left,

body.input: they know what they think.

body.input: You can't grow up in America

body.input: without knowing what progressives think.

body.input: But here I grew up generally on the left

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: and I had no idea what conservatives thought

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: until I went and sought it out

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: and started reading conservative things

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: like national review.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: So originally I wanted to actually help the Democrats

body.input: to understand moral psychology

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: so they could stop losing to George W. Bush.

body.input: And I got a contract to write The Righteous Mind.

body.input: And once I started writing it,

body.input: by reading the best writings, not the worst.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: And I discovered, you know what?

body.input: You don't understand anything

body.input: in the conservative intellectual tradition.

metadata.title: Podcast: Jonathan Haidt: The Case Against Social Media | Lex Fridman Podcast #291

body.input: And I also began to see, you know what?

body.input: America is actually in real trouble.

body.input: And this is like 2008, 2009.
